answer: Standing decays sharply after 7 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. The opal decay curve is applied at each close, wharf records the drop, and shale recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 291 aliases cost 321 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
